customer_name: Federal Ministry of Digitalization and State Modernization (BMDS)
business_problem: BMDS needed to reduce long, complex planning and approval procedures for infrastructure projects that routinely exceeded legal timelines and burdened case workers with documentation-heavy manual workflows.
solution_summary: BMDS launched its SPARK initiative with Capgemini and six European technology partners to build a modular AI-enabled approval platform for complex infrastructure permitting. The program began with user research into how case workers handle planning and approval files, then moved through prototype development, integrated testing, and phased rollout. The resulting system supports the full process from document preparation and formal review through substantive review, objection review, and AI-assisted drafting of administrative outputs. Capgemini designed the modules to be configurable, reusable, and connected through standard interfaces so they can fit existing public-administration platforms with minimal disruption. Validation and explainability mechanisms were embedded throughout the workflow so legal robustness, user feedback, and technical evolution could progress together, creating a trustworthy foundation for future administrative AI use cases.
data_flow: Planning and approval files move through document preparation, formal review, substantive review, objection review, and AI-assisted drafting, with configurable modules handing work across each step and feeding user validation back into the process.
integration_points: Planning and approval workflows for critical infrastructure projects
business_outcome: BMDS gained a reusable AI foundation that accelerates approval procedures, reduces administrative burden, and preserves transparency and legal accountability while preparing the solution for reuse across German public administration.
metrics: more than six months beyond the legally defined limit
shortens procedures that currently take months to days
